newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude ends up on technicals, bullish views.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude ends up on technicals, bullish views.

text.p: NYMEX crude ended with sharp gains Thursday as bullish sentiment underpinned by strong technicals and tight supplies eclipsed the nearing prospect of Iraqi oil on the market.

"Crude looks really strong. It went down to around $25.00, and it popped right back up," said Thomas Blakeslee, analyst with Cargill Investor Services, noting prompt crude's technical strength after it broke its contract high of $25.20.
January crude settled 78 cents higher at $25.58 a barrel. Traders also noted crude supplies are tight when refinery runs are high.

The most recent oil inventory data from the American Petroleum Institute (API) shows crude stocks 17.9 million barrels below a year ago when demand for crude to make refined products in Asia is also increasing, analysts noted. The API data released Tuesday shows refinery utilization rates at 93.7 percent.

January heating oil ended up 1.54 cents a gallon at 75.11 cents while January gasoline finished 1.44 cents a gallon higher at 69.68 cents. A strike by oil workers in France spurred gains in gas oil futures on London's IPE which in turn helped heating oil prices, dealers said.
Gas oil is the European equivalent of heating oil.

The strike at three refineries owned French oil giant Elf Aquitaine continued into its second week Thursday. Union officials said they would discuss Elf's proposals after talks between them Thursday. The strike has crippled a quarter of French refinery capacity and three quarters of Elf's European refinery network.
Analysts and traders have said the strike could cut into U.S. gasoline imports as Europe may now have to hold on to whatever gasoline it has.
"Crude runs are high. The strike has been a big plus for gasoline all week, and thus a big plus for crude," said John Saucer, analyst with Smith Barney.

After Jan crude broke its contract high and key technical resistance of $25.20, traders said it has the momentum to test the $25.70, a major shelf of resistance on crude's spot continuation chart. From there, it faces major resistance of $26.10, crude's post-Gulf War high made October 22.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
